observations: Vintage treadle sewing machine mounted in a wooden folding cabinet/table.
Cast iron treadle base with decorative scroll-work visible in photos 0-2.
Machine body is black with gold floral/scroll decoration, consistent with older Chinese-made machines.
Photo 3 shows a small black box (motor) attached to the machine head with a cable, and Chinese characters plus English text reading 'MADE IN THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA' on the arm.
Wooden cabinet shows surface wear, scratches, and some discoloration on the lid in photo 2.
Two small drawers are visible on either side of the machine bed.
No power cord, foot pedal, or plug is clearly visible in any photo.
No stitching sample, running video, or close-up of the motor's wiring/condition is provided.

identity.kind: treadle sewing machine with attached electric motor (vintage cabinet style)
read_from: photo 3 (Chinese/English manufacturing text, no brand name legible)

claims.evidence: No 'Butterfly' brand name or logo is legible in any photo; only generic 'Made in PRC' text is visible in photo 3.
Photo 3 shows a small motor attached to the machine head, but no video or demonstration shows it running or the treadle functioning.

risks.risk: Motor may not power on or may have damaged wiring
risks.proof: Video of the motor running with the machine stitching, or close-up photo of the motor's plug and wiring

risks.risk: Treadle mechanism (belt, pedal, linkage) may be seized, missing, or broken
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the leather/belt drive and a photo or clip of the treadle being pedaled

risks.risk: Missing accessories (bobbins, needles, power cord, foot pedal controller)
risks.proof: Photo of accessory box/drawer contents and the power cord/pedal

risks.risk: Cabinet/table structural integrity (veneer peeling, drawer function, wood rot)
risks.proof: Close-up photos of drawer slides, underside of table, and any visible damage
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic-only, structural condition unknown

risks.risk: Electrical safety of the motor (exposed wires, no proper casing)
risks.proof: Clear photo of the motor's wiring and plug/casing

proof_requests: Video of the machine being pedaled (treadle) and/or the motor running, showing actual stitching
Close-up photo of any brand nameplate or decal legible enough to confirm 'Butterfly' or other maker
Photo of the power cord, plug, and foot pedal/motor controller if included
Photo of drawer interiors showing included accessories (bobbins, needles, manual)
Close-up of the treadle belt and leg joints for wear or breakage
response.reason: The item is clearly a vintage treadle sewing machine with an attached electric motor in a wooden cabinet, but no brand name is legible and no proof of working condition, motor function, or completeness is shown, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-verified, possibly non-functional antique machine.
